sample_unit: nutrition-related clinical issues (ChatGPT responses compared with guidelines; 5 expert raters)

links.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT nutrition recommendations with CSCO, CNS and ESPEN guidelines
links.effect: ChatGPT aligned with at least one guideline in 50.0–64.3% of cases (highest for dysphagia, 64.3%). Guidelines scored higher for evidence-based support (4.9/5) and clinical feasibility (4.7/5).
links.quote: ChatGPT recommendations aligned with at least one guideline in 50.0–64.3% of cases, highest for dysphagia (64.3%), and included general strategies such as small frequent meals, texture modification, hydration, and high-protein/high-calorie intake.

links.outcome: Readability (Flesch–Kincaid grade) of ChatGPT outputs versus guidelines
links.effect: ChatGPT Flesch–Kincaid grade 12.9–14.2 versus guidelines 17.9–20.5; clarity 4.5 vs 3.2. ChatGPT is more readable than guidelines but still at a high grade level.
links.quote: ChatGPT exhibited superior patient-centered performance in clarity (4.5 vs 3.2) and self-management guidance (4.6 vs 3.0) and demonstrated more concise, readable content (Flesch–Kincaid grade 12.9–14.2) compared with guidelines (17.9–20.5).

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT-generated nutritional guidance against established clinical guidelines via expert evaluation, readability metrics, and semantic similarity without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
